To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GRAPES‐3 muon telescope has successfully measured the Swinson flow at a rigidity of ∽100 GeV and the radial density gradient at 77 GeV, for the first time.
the amplitude and the phase of the Swinson effect have been measured with a precision of 0.8% and 5 min, respectively, for the first time.
the amplitude and phase of the Swinson Flow and the radial density gradient have been measured with high precision using the GRAPES 3 muon telescope.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the radial density profile of the galactic component of cosmic rays in the heliospheric region, which is a subject of considerable importance in the field of cosmic ray research and astrophysics.
the measurement of the radial density profile of cosmic ray in heliosphere by using the GRAPES 3 data.
the study of the radial density profile of galactic cosmic rays in heliocentric distance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radial density gradient is 0.65 ± 0·02% AU −1 and the phase of the maximum Swinson flow is (17.70 ± 0·05) h.

the GRAPES–3 experiment has measured for the first time, the Swinson flow with an accuracy of ∼1%, and the associated radial density gradient of galactic cosmic rays in the heliosheath with an accuracy of 20% at a rigidity of ∣ Z × B∣  ≈ 77 GV.
the GRAPES experiment has provided the most definitive evidence for the radial density gradient and the Swinson flow of cosmic rays within the helioshere.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the radial anisotropies in the cosmic ray flux in heliosphere have been measured by the GRAPSES-3 experiment and the underlying radial gradient of the galatic cosmic rays in heliohpere has been estimated for the first time.
the GRAPES–3 experiment is the first experiment to measure the radial density gradient and Swinson flow in the heliospheric region at a relatively high cosmic ray energy.
the radial density gradient was found to be consistent with the theoretical predictions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GRAPES experiment offers a powerful tool to probe the heliosphere in situ and measure the radial gradient of cosmic ray flux in heliosphere.
the GRAPES–3 experiment can be used for measuring the Swinson flow with a precision of 0.001% which is a factor of ∼10 more precise than the current measurements.
GRAPES-2/3 is a powerful instrument to measure the radial density gradient and the Swinson flow in the heliosheath.
